# ECF_ROADMAP.md

# Purpose

This document defines the planned evolution of the Engineering Control Framework (ECF).

The roadmap is capability-driven rather than feature-driven.

Each version of ECF introduces new engineering capabilities while preserving the framework's architectural principles.

ECF evolves through experience gained from real software projects.

---

# Roadmap Philosophy

ECF follows five principles for evolution.

## 1. Validate Before Expanding

Every new capability should first be validated through real engineering work.

Ideas are not sufficient justification for expanding the framework.

---

## 2. Preserve Simplicity

Every new concept increases framework complexity.

New concepts should be introduced only when existing concepts cannot reasonably represent the problem.

---

## 3. Maintain Backward Compatibility

Projects should be able to adopt newer versions of ECF incrementally.

Breaking changes should be rare and well documented.

---

## 4. Framework Before Tooling

ECF defines engineering.

Tools implement ECF.

The framework should remain independent of any specific AI provider, IDE, programming language, or platform.

---

## 5. Dogfood Everything

ECF should evolve by engineering itself using ECF.

The framework should never ask projects to follow practices that ECF itself does not follow.

---

# Version 0.1 — Foundation

## Goal

Establish the conceptual foundation of ECF.

## Capabilities

* Framework identity
* Engineering philosophy
* Meta-model
* Framework architecture
* Core principles
* Standards model
* Canonical artifact model
* Knowledge Transformation model

## Deliverables

* README
* FOUNDATION
* FRAMEWORK_ARCHITECTURE
* ECF_META_MODEL
* ARTIFACT_STANDARD
* DIAGRAM_STANDARD
* KNOWLEDGE_TRANSFORMATION_MODEL

## Explicit Non-Goals

* AI orchestration
* Automation
* CLI tooling
* Code generation
* IDE integration

---

* Review catalog

## Capabilities

* Stable templates
* Adoption guide
* Migration guide
* Version compatibility
* Reference implementations

## Deliverables

* ECF v1.0 release

---

# Future Vision (Beyond 1.0)

Potential future directions include:

* Engineering Intermediate Representation (EIR)
* Engineering validation engine
* Automated standards compliance
* Artifact dependency analysis
* Multi-project governance
* Framework plugins
* Engineering language server
* Engineering knowledge graph
* Framework marketplace

These ideas remain exploratory and should be validated through practical experience before entering the roadmap.

---

# Release Criteria

A version is complete only when:

* all planned capabilities are implemented
* documentation is complete
* reference examples exist
* framework changes have been reviewed
* framework quality gates pass
* at least one real project successfully adopts the version

---

# Framework Success

ECF succeeds when projects using it demonstrate:

* higher engineering confidence
* better engineering artifacts
* more consistent decision-making
* clearer architecture
* predictable AI collaboration
* reusable engineering knowledge
* lower onboarding effort
* reduced engineering risk

The ultimate measure of ECF is not the quality of the framework itself.

The ultimate measure is the quality of the software engineered using it.
